history.period: Late 15th century CE (built by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: this temple is NOT at Kamalpur — it stands at Kasba village (Kamalasagar), Bishalgarh subdivision, Sepahijala district, ~27-32 km south of Agartala, directly on the India-Bangladesh border; Kamalpur is a different town ~160 km away in Dhalai district. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name — corrected to Tripura. OVERLAP: an existing dataset file 'kamalasagar-kali-temple-kasba' (1040.json) already covers this same temple — keep-or-merge decision needed. The shrine was built on a hill-top in the late 15th century by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya (one source says work was started by Maharaja Kalyan Manikya — conflict, unverified); the Kamalasagar lake in front was dug by Dhanya Manikya and named after his wife Kamaladevi, and the place was anciently known as Kamalagarh/Koilagarh, later renamed Kasba. The main idol is actually a 15th-century sandstone Dasabhuja (ten-handed) Durga / Mahishasurmardini, but because the base platform bears an image of Shiva it is worshipped as Maa Kali; a Shivalinga sculpture stands at the idol's feet. The temple draws devotees from both India and Bangladesh and sits close enough to the border fence that Bangladeshi territory is visible from the complex.

name: Kamalasagar Kali Temple
town_description: Kasba is a border village in Bishalgarh subdivision, Sepahijala district, right on the India-Bangladesh border about 27-32 km south of Agartala. It is known for the hill-top Kasba Kali Temple overlooking the historic Kamalasagar lake, one of Tripura's most visited Shakti shrines.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~32 km)
travel.road: Buses/small vehicles from Agartala to Rastarmatha, Bishalgarh, then auto/rickshaw to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter); Sundays are busy
